cells.value:
Application Demonstrations are designed for the Delivery Consultant and Solution Architect to conduct hands on demonstrations walking client Super Users through the completed applications/integrations, end-to-end. Ideally, we group the demonstrations by process group/application set (Inbound, Inventory, Outbound). Best practice is to perform the walk through on customer devices. Leverage the approved test scripts as part of our walkthrough. Cloud Inventory to perform any issue remediation or address training items as needed. Any issues will be documented as an issue and tracked in Jira, associated with the application/integration where the problem occurred (use the 'Bug' issue type, but please note this does not indicate a product bug). These demonstrations are to occur iteratively throughout the development cycle as components of the process groups/applications sets are completed. 
Allows client Super Users & impacted customer stakeholders first hand exposure to the solutions and allows for feedback prior to customer testing/UAT. The goal is to get feedback as early as possible to allow enough time to make adjustments as needed. Note: any new requirements or out of scope changes need to be raised to customer PM and sponsor for CO approval before any action is taken to address them.

cells.value:
The Solution Workshop / Conference Room Pilot is typically an on-site event where the SA, DC, and PM assist the customer to run through the Cloud Inventory solution we have created end-to-end, leveraging the customer-built test scripts. The customer super users will be executing the transactions on their devices/scanners that will be used in production. 
This exercise should be used for the Cloud Inventory team to train the super users on how to use the system, how to troubleshoot issues, and enable them to train the remaining UAT users and be the initial triage layer before reporrting issues back to Cloud Inventory. This is the intial transfer of ownership of the solution from Cloud Inventory to the customer.

values.D10: Project management admin time is a bucket of hours is used to complete various tasks like weekly meetings, project status reports & any project planning events that take place.
values.E10: To provide project managers allotted time to complete project admin work through the lifecycle of a project.
values.D12: The internal project kickoff is an event for net new projects involving the full sales team, project team & executive sponsors with the goal of understanding full details of the sales cycle. Topics include who our competition was, were there partners involved, what the big selling points were, why they chose DSI, was there a go-live date discussed, what kind of hardware are they running, any special concessions that were made, etc.
values.E12: Ensure entire internal team understands what occurred in the sales cycle & to be prepared going into kickoff meeting. Internal project team identified & prepped for client kickoff meeting.
values.D13: This meeting is scheduled by the account executive & is an intimate meeting with the client, account executive, client success manager & project manager. The purpose of this call is to introduce the project manager with the end goal of scheduling the project kickoff meeting.
values.E13: Ensures project team has steps in place to get kickoff meeting scheduled. Goal is to keep the excitement level high with customer.
values.B17: Establish Customer Team and Escalation Paths
values.B19: Log Infrastructure JIRA ticket for ADW/Install
values.B20: Architecture Design Workshop (ADW) & Architecture Design Document (ADD)
values.D20: The architecture design workshop is led by an infrastructure consultant, implementation leader & meant for customer's technical team. Usually includes customer roles: IT director or system admin. Goals are to talk through security, printing infrastructure setup & connectivity to Cloud Inventory, ports to open, etc. Resulting document is Architecture Design Documentation.
values.E20: Ensure customer is set up for success regarding security access, printing infrastructure & cloud connectivity.
values.B21: Confirm ERP Version/Release (i.e. tools release, 32- vs. 64-bit)
values.B22: Open CSC ticket to supply customer with product package associated with their ERP version (i.e. ASUs, BAPIs) if needed
values.B23: Request the data in the F9670 Software Update Master table, so ESU/ASU can be verified
values.B24: Provide Customer Installation Master to Customer
values.B25: Provide Architecture Design Document to Customer
values.D27: High level project plan based on initial scope.
values.E27: Allows project team(s) to better visualize project timeline.
values.D29: This is done to hold correct resource. Not being scheduled by task at this point.
values.E29: Ensures resourcing can be as associate as possible as early in project as possible.
values.B30: Request VPN & ERP Access / Onboarding Requirements
values.D31: Work with the customer to get necessary access for all resources that will be working on the implementation
values.E31: Allows our consultants to work directly on the customers network for devlopment and testing purposes.
values.B32: Create Shared Folder and Begin Project Status Reporting
values.D32: The project status reporting is a weekly report that the project manager sends out. This report follows an existing template. This report is sent to account executive, the CSM, the executive sponsor, Technical Sponsor, PMO Manager, SA & DC.
values.E32: Ensure entire project team is updated on weekly project changes.
values.B33: Finalize Customer Kickoff Presentation with Customer PM
values.D34: Project kickoff meeting is led by the implementation leader & is focused on a presentation to customer team (usually 1-2 hours long). Best practice is to have this event on site. This includes the entire internal project team, sales team & customer team. Goal is to ensure customer is totally confident with implementation team & plan. If Delivery Consultant is resourced to project at this points its nice to have them listen in.
values.E34: Ensure customer is totally confident with implementation team & plan.
values.D35: Scheduled weekly project calls are led by implementation leader & meant for the customer project team. CSMs are also included. The purpose of these calls is to review project plan, budget, roadblocks, or immediate next steps, etc.
values.E35: Ensure all project teams are in sync & in agreement on project status
values.D36: Executive alignment calls are facilitated & scheduled by the project manager. But will only include the executive sponsors both on the client and DSI side.
values.E36: Ensure executives are in communication during project life cycle.
values.D37: Customer Administrative training is purely self-paced online trading the that the customer admin is requried to complete. This is an important steps & must be completed prior to any build starting. Customer should also be encouraged to start using DSI document portal & community pages as they ar a great tool at this point in the project.
values.E37: Ensure client admin users are given the basic training they need to be successful at this point in the project. Allows customer to get engaged via DSI Doc Portal & DSI Community pages.
values.D38: The customer gateway and infrastructure set up is a customer task to get any of the action items that they have coming out of that architecture Design workshop completed. Resulting actions might be setting up a gateway server, gaining access to network for printing, or if they're hosting any on prem ERPs we’ll need all access setup correctly for the install.
values.E38: Ensure customer has correct infrastructure in place prior to solution install occurring.
values.B39: Not Included - EPP Print Bridge Installation
values.D39: This task is for the installation of the EPP print bridge (if required).This is typically used in the scenario where MEP is hosted in the cloud or in a different environment than where the printers are phsyically located and used to establish the connection between the two separate networks.
values.D40: CloudOps & infrastructure handles theMEP install. This task is the customer tenant being provisioned & the actual software installed.
values.E40: Ensure that the customer install contains MEPand EPP.
values.B42: Not Included - Ensure Language Text Files are Migrated
values.B44: Not Included - Enterprise Printing Platform Installation
values.B46: Not Included - Base Application Package Install
values.D48: The site visit & walkthrough are for the Solution Architect, Project Manager, and Delivery Consultant (optional - depends on nature of the project). This event is to allow time to walk through client warehouse/facility, to identify their processes and get an understanding for how they're going to be using the solution. Findings are documented in real time.
values.E48: Ensure project team understands customers physical facility layout & can better visualize how software will be utilized.
values.D49:
As a part of the site visit & walkthrough, detailed notes are taken. Generally, those notes are compiled & used to complete the solution Orientation session. A solution orientation session is where CI resources walk through the baselie applications/solution with the customer logged in to base Cloud Inventory following along.

The flow of a Solution orientation session should be similar from project to project but should call out specifically where likely system changes will occur. This should be a scripted session & often serves as a training event to get client acclimated to base Cloud Inventory transactions.
values.E49: Ensure client has basic navigation skills in Cloud Inventory & has been oriented as to how the base transactions work. Client has been shown where customizations are likely to occur.
values.D50: The Pacejet Requirements session is a joint meeting with Pacejet, Cloud Inventory and the customer. It is advised that Cloud Inventory and Pacejet have a discussion following the requirements gathering session to review the requirements captured prior to hosting the call with the customer.
values.D51: Document created as a result of discussions that occurred at the Solution Orientation Session. Analysis to be used at executive alignment calls as needed.
values.E51: Ensure out of scope topics are captured effectively.
values.B52: Not Included - Business Requirement Document (BRD) Creation & Review Sessions
values.C52: SA, Product Manager, Customer Project Teams
values.D52: BRD review sessions are typically led by the Solution Architect, Team Lead/Project Lead, Project Managers, & Delivery Consultant (optional). Goal is to work together to make sure customer fully understand the business requirements document and working towards sign off. And those are usually multiple (2-3) sessions to work through the BRD & get it ready for signoff.
values.E52: Ensure client is fully aware of the BRD components & working towards document signoff.
values.B53: Not Included - Business Requirement Document (BRD) Sign Off
values.D53: CI sends the final draft of the BRD with a signature block to the signatory on the customer side and they execute it. Once signed any additional changes will result in change orders.
values.E53: Ensure client has signed BRD document to move project forward.
values.D54: This is to take the high-level project plan and dates that we have been discussing up to this point, putting it into a final project plan with accurate resources, contingencies built in and then work with the customer project team to make sure that lines up with their dates, their resources, their expectations, and then will commit to the go live date and final project plan.
values.E54: Ensure initial project dates & requirements are accounted for in a final project plan that also aligns with client needs.
values.D58: Solution design is time for the solution architect to complete design work on any customizations identified as part of the BRD.
values.E58: Ensure time allotted for design work to occur based on customer requirements.
values.B59: Not Included - CI to Write Test Scripts (did not opt-in)
values.D60: Client is to own the creation of test scripts. Typically, we will help Customer build test scripts based off the BRD and ensure the test cases cover end to end processes.
values.E60: Ensure client is comfortable writing test scripts & has capacity to do so. Ensure standard test scripts from dev/product team are made avaialble to client.
values.D61: Solution Architects will review the final customer test scripts and ensure they line up with the BRD and complete sign off. If this is not getting done, then it needs to be raised to the exec sponsors.
values.E61: Ensure alignment on client created test scripts.
values.B62: Not Included - Internal Solution Design Review
values.D62: CI internal task, CI team works to ensure that documented ADO processes were in fact the best way too solve for client issue/requests & identified problem were solved in an efficient way. CI team will be reviewing ADO tool directly.
values.E62: Ensure alignment on project design documentation prior to project moving to next phase.
values.D66: Delivery Consultant works with the client to train them on how to get  scanners configured appropriately in accordance with the SOW, load the DSI mobile client & execute mobile apps on scanners. Ensure scanner requirements are identified, issues documented & configuration started.
values.D67: Delivery Consultant works to get printers setup in EPP per SOW. Ensure customer admin understand show to setup printers in MEP and EPP, and that the customer is actively working to test each type of printer model to be used in production and that the connection is established.
values.B68: Not Included - Ensure Temporary Licenses are in Place for New MEP Instance
values.D68: For upgrade projects, PM to work with Infrastructure Consultant, Account Executive, and CSC to ensure there are sufficient licenses in place for the new instance of MEP - both from a user licenses standpoint and platform license standpoint.
values.B69: Not Included - Verify List of Apps to be Migrated
values.D69: PM and Delivery Consultant to ensure the applications called out in the SOW match what the customer expects to be migrated. If additional applications are requested to be migrated, work with the customer and Account Executive through the change order process before migrating the additional applications.
values.B70: Review Apps with Data Replication with Project Lead Prior to Migration (if applicable)
values.D70: For upgrade projects, if there are any applications to be migrated that include data replication, have the Delivery Consultant work with the Project/Team Lead to review the Data Replication Rules, Tables, and Schedules prior to migrating the applications to ensure they migrate properly.
values.D115: This encompasses all modification work done with Cloud Inventory Applications per the requirements & design documents.
values.E115: Allows Delivery Consultant time & tracking for all app/system modification.
values.B213: Not Included - Application Developer Training (did not opt-in)
values.B215: Unit Testing & QA  (hours included in application and/or upgrade estimates above)
values.D215: This task is for the Delivery Consultant to unit test the application(s) prior to hand-off to the customer for testing, leveraging the approved tset scripts for each application. For upgrade projects, unit testing is typically fairly limited and focuses on surface testing (i.e. the apps publish, can open without error, etc.) Unit Testing hours estimates are included in the individual application line items listed above.
values.D216: Completed with technical leadership team, full review of applications built by Delivery Consultants. Code review and demo with the technical leadership team
values.E216: Ensure applications are created and perform as designed; are functioning as intended without error.
values.D217: Customer task in which they work to create all users & roles as needed. DC to validate that the customer admin has set up users and roles correctly, typically results in Delivery Consultant assisting in the process.
values.E217: Ensure client has users & roles created correctly in preparation for go-live.
values.D218: Share an issues log and begin assigning issues to resources.
values.E218: Ensure client domain issues are captured & tracked correctly.
values.C219: PM DC Customer Super users  Pace Jet
values.D219: This task is for the Delivery Consultant to demonstrate the Pacejet solution (if in scope) with the customer and confirm the solution is working as expected prior to UAT.
values.B220: Confirm resourcing & submit requests for UAT support (2-weeks prior to UAT)
values.D220: This task is for the PM to work with the customer to confirm UAT timing & details (e.g., on-site vs remote, testing plan/schedule, etc.) and align CI resources appropriately to support the event. Once the details are finalized, the PM will submit the necessary resource requests to ensure the event is supported appropriately.
values.D221:
Application Demonstrations are designed for the Delivery Consultant and Solution Architect to conduct hands on demonstrations walking client Super Users through the completed applications/integrations, end-to-end. Ideally, we group the demonstrations by process group/application set (Inbound, Inventory, Outbound). Best practice is to perform the walk through on customer devices. Leverage the approved test scripts as part of our walkthrough. Cloud Inventory to perform any issue remediation or address training items as needed. Any issues will be documented as an issue and tracked in Jira, associated with the application/integration where the problem occurred (use the 'Bug' issue type, but please note this does not indicate a product bug). These demonstrations are to occur iteratively throughout the development cycle as components of the process groups/applications sets are completed. 
Allows client Super Users & impacted customer stakeholders first hand exposure to the solutions and allows for feedback prior to customer testing/UAT. The goal is to get feedback as early as possible to allow enough time to make adjustments as needed. Note: any new requirements or out of scope changes need to be raised to customer PM and sponsor for CO approval before any action is taken to address them.
values.D222:
Review any/all remediation work that has occurred following the demonstrations to ensure solution set is ready for the Conference Room Pilot. Addressed items must be reviewed internally and if time allows, should be re-presented to the customer prior to the Conference Room Pilot.
Ensure that all takeaways from the initial solution workshops have been addressed in order to have a successful work.
values.B223: Not Included - Solution Workshop / Conference Room Pilot and Train the Trainer
values.D223:
The Solution Workshop / Conference Room Pilot is typically an on-site event where the SA, DC, and PM assist the customer to run through the Cloud Inventory solution we have created end-to-end, leveraging the customer-built test scripts. The customer super users will be executing the transactions on their devices/scanners that will be used in production. 
This exercise should be used for the Cloud Inventory team to train the super users on how to use the system, how to troubleshoot issues, and enable them to train the remaining UAT users and be the initial triage layer before reporrting issues back to Cloud Inventory. This is the intial transfer of ownership of the solution from Cloud Inventory to the customer.
values.D224: Delivery consultant promotes applications accordingly with goal to validate they are working correctly in the customer envionment prior to UAT. This task may occur prior to the application demonstrations and subsequent tasks, depending on the project and state of the associated ERP environments.
values.D225: This  task is for the PM to work with the Account Executive, Delivery Consultant, CSC, anad customer to confirm the appropriate amount of user or device licenses are configured in the Test environment prior to testing. The goal is to ensure adequate licenses are available to match the number of users that will be testing as well as for the consultant(s) suporting the event.
values.B229: Confirm resourcing & submit requests for Go-live support (2-weeks prior to Go-live)
values.D229: This task is for the PM to work with the customer to confirm Go-live timing & details (e.g., on-site vs remote, cutover plan/schedule, etc.) and align CI resources appropriately to support the event. Once the details are finalized, the PM will submit the necessary resource requests to ensure the event is supported appropriately.
values.B230: Not Included - Develop End User Documentation (did not opt-in)
values.D230: This is an add-on task customers can opt-in to where a CI Delivery Consultant creates end-user documentation / training guides on how to use the applications that are being implemented as part of the project. If a customer does not opt-in to this deliverable, PM needs to work with the customer to ensure they have an adequate training plan in place prior to testing and cutover.
values.B231: Select & Introduce User Acceptance Testing (UAT) Users
values.D231: Customer to select and train the User Acceptance Testing users. These users play a part in the final validation of the software. This training likely has large overlap with Solution workshop training events.
values.E231: Ensure client has identified who the UAT users will be & that they are comfortable navigating the solution effectively.
values.D232: Create & finalize detailed UAT agenda outlining what apps are being tested & when with the customer team. Create PPT presentation for user testing kickoff event.
values.E232: Ensure UAT event is outlined & app testing sequence identified.
values.D233: This task is for the Solution Architect, Delivery Consultant, and PM to work with the customer to ensure enough data is prepared for the UAT testing team to execute all of the UAT test scripts during the UAT window.
values.D234: User Acceptance Testing event is designed to allow client users to test their solutions on the floor with devices setup and printers configured. Delivery Consultant are asked to support as issues might arise & all issues get put on an issues log and assigned to the dedicated resource to remediate. PM & DC will facilitate the session and issues logging.
values.E234: Ensures client is hands on testing their solution & logging any issues that are found.
values.D237: Once User Acceptance Testing is complete, client will sign off confirming issues are resolved & event is complete.
values.E237: Provides written confirmation & client agreement the event was successful.
values.D238: Project manager schedules meeting with Customer Support Center team. This introduction meeting is a quick introduction & presentation covering solution support. This meeting occurs prior to any applications going into client’s production envionment.
values.E238: Serves as customers first look at post go-live support structure & allows for questions to ensure client is confident in support process.
values.B239: Not Included - CI Led End User Training (did not opt-in)
values.D239: This is an add-on task customers can opt-in to where a CI Delivery Consultant provides training to the end user group on how to use the applications that are being implemented as part of the project. If a customer does not opt-in to this deliverable, PM needs to work with the customer to ensure they have an adequate training plan in place prior to testing and cutover.
values.D240: Previously trained client Trainers & Super Users to complete all additional customer End User Training.
values.E240: Ensure customer has a plan to successfully train all end users & completes training on time for all new solutions.
values.D242: The platform limited load test is conducted by the Infrastructure Consultant in collaboration with the customer. The goal of the exercise is to simulate the production volume plus additional load to ensure performance is stable prior to production go-live.
values.D243: Go-Live Readiness Assessment is a process in which the project manager walks through the go-live plan with the client project team to ensure full alignment. Topics covered include a clear communication plan to report issues, a roll-back plan, onsite support logistics, etc.
values.E243: Ensures client is well supported at go-live & has contingency plans in place.
values.D244: Promote apps, validate applications are working an updating ERP as expected.
values.E244: Ensure the solution is ready for users to begin using in the production environment.
values.D248: Meeting to build the Go-Live agenda. Schedule go-live cutover, aligning resources & creating agenda for go-live.
values.E248: Ensure Go-Live plan is communicated & all teams are aligned on strategy.
values.D249: Go-Live support period begins once (1) UAT signoff & (2) Go-Live readiness signoff occur. DSI will begin moving applications into production & cutting over the data. Typically, this is one week on site and one week remote.
values.E249: Provide client with support as needed during agreed upon go-live support window.
values.D250: Typically done a few weeks post go-live & once client is stable. This is a secondary meeting with CSC to complete formal transition in closing out the project.
values.E250: Provides customer exact workflow for solution issue support following project closure.
values.D251: Following CSC transition, the customer signs project closure document & project is closed.
values.E251: Provides written confirmation & client agreement the project was successful.
values.D252: This is the internal retrospective to review what went well and what didn't go well to evaluate how we can improve processes/procedures for future implementations. There is a restrospective template in confluence we should use for this.

The Sales to Delivery Handoff is an event for new projects involving the full sales team, project team & executive sponsors with the goal of understanding full details of the sales cycle. Topics include who our competition was, were there partners involved, what the big selling points were, why they chose Cloud Inventory, was there a go-live date discussed, what kind of hardware are they running, any special concessions that were made, etc. Sales should fill out the sales to delivery handoff document, walk PSO through it, and lead this meeting.
Ensure entire internal team understands what occurred in the sales cycle & to be prepared going into kickoff meeting. Internal project team identified & prepped for client kickoff meeting.

cells.value:
Customer Administrative training is purely self-paced online training the that the customer admin is requried to complete. This is an important steps & must be completed prior to any testing starting. PM and CI team need to be sure to stress the importance of thsi training and the customer's system administration role. They will be responsible for monitoring integrations, transactions, triaging questions and issues, etc. If this role cannot be fulfilled by the customer, we should discuss long-term strategy internally and then with the customer and determine if additional service offerings are needed. Customer should also be encouraged to start using Cloud Inventory documentation portal & community pages as they are a great tool at this point in the project. The PM should check with the AE on the number of training licenses provided as part of the sale. Once the number of licenses and the specific users who will be going through the training are identified, the PM will need to create an access request in service desk (Service Desk > Service Catalog > Training > LMS User Access) https://servicedesk.nextworld.net/support/catalog/items/345
Ensure client admin users are given the basic training they need to be successful at this point in the project. Allows customer to get engaged via Cloud Inventory Doc Portal & Cloud Inventory Community pages.

cells.value:
Application Demonstrations are designed for the Delivery Consultant and Solution Architect to conduct hands on demonstrations walking client Super Users through the completed applications/integrations, end-to-end. Ideally, we group the demonstrations by process group/application set (Inbound, Inventory, Outbound). Best practice is to perform the walk through on customer devices. Leverage the approved test scripts as part of our walkthrough. Cloud Inventory to perform any issue remediation or address training items as needed. Any issues will be documented as an issue and tracked in Jira, associated with the application/integration where the problem occurred (use the 'Bug' issue type, but please note this does not indicate a product bug). These demonstrations are to occur iteratively throughout the development cycle as components of the process groups/applications sets are completed. 
Allows client Super Users & impacted customer stakeholders first hand exposure to the solutions and allows for feedback prior to customer testing/UAT. The goal is to get feedback as early as possible to allow enough time to make adjustments as needed. Note: any new requirements or out of scope changes need to be raised to customer PM and sponsor for CO approval before any action is taken to address them.

cells.value:
The Solution Workshop / Conference Room Pilot is typically an on-site event where the SA, DC, and PM assist the customer to run through the Cloud Inventory solution we have created end-to-end, leveraging the customer-built test scripts. The customer super users will be executing the transactions on their devices/scanners that will be used in production. 
This exercise should be used for the Cloud Inventory team to train the super users on how to use the system, how to troubleshoot issues, and enable them to train the remaining UAT users and be the initial triage layer before reporrting issues back to Cloud Inventory. This is the intial transfer of ownership of the solution from Cloud Inventory to the customer.

values.D3: This task is for the time it takes to review the scope and set up the OpenAir project tasks, JIRA/Excel project plan, schedule initial meetings, etc.
values.D4:
The Sales to Delivery Handoff is an event for new projects involving the full sales team, project team & executive sponsors with the goal of understanding full details of the sales cycle. Topics include who our competition was, were there partners involved, what the big selling points were, why they chose Cloud Inventory, was there a go-live date discussed, what kind of hardware are they running, any special concessions that were made, etc. Sales should fill out the sales to delivery handoff document, walk PSO through it, and lead this meeting.
Ensure entire internal team understands what occurred in the sales cycle & to be prepared going into kickoff meeting. Internal project team identified & prepped for client kickoff meeting.
values.D5:
This meeting is scheduled by the account executive & is an intimate meeting with the client, account executive, client success manager & project manager. The purpose of this call is to introduce the project manager with the end goal of scheduling the project kickoff meeting.
Ensures project team has steps in place to get kickoff meeting scheduled. Goal is to keep the excitement level high with customer.
values.D6:
This meeting is scheduled as a follow up to the customer introduction as an avenue for the PMs of both teams to finalize the kickoff presentation, request necessary ERP or VPN access, and coordinate the architecture design workshop if it was not scheduled directly following the customer introduction.
Ensure both teams are ready to jointly present the kickoff slides, the customer is working to provide ERP/VPN access, and that the ADW is scheduled.
values.H6: Log Infrastructure JIRA ticket for ADW/Install
values.L6: Finalize Customer Kickoff Presentation with Customer PM
values.D7: During the PM Intro/Planning meeting, work with the customer PM to define (if not already defined) what will make this project successful from the customer's perspective. This is generally the "why" the customer selected one or more of our products. We will use this in our kickoff deck and should be a way to measure the success of the project/implementation.
values.D8: During the PM Intro/Planning meeting, work with the customer PM to define the high-level schedule. Discuss any key milestone dates, such as UAT or Go-live, as well as any black-out periods for the customer's business.
values.C9: Establish Customer Team and Escalation Paths
values.D9: During the PM Intro/Planning meeting, introduce the customer PM to the Customer Contacts by Role document and work with them to explain our internal escalation paths.
values.D10: During the PM Intro/Planning meeting, work with the customer PM to establish a weekly cadence (or my frequent depending on the project) to hold status calls.
values.C11: Log Infrastructure JIRA ticket for ADW/Install
values.D11: PM to log a ticket in Jira to have the Infrastructure team assign a resource to conduct the ADW and subsequent install.
values.H11: Architecture Design Workshop (ADW) & Architecture Design Document (ADD)
values.C12: Architecture Design Workshop (ADW) & Architecture Design Document (ADD)
values.D12:
The architecture design workshop is led by an infrastructure consultant, project manager & meant for customer's technical team. Usually includes customer roles: IT director or system admin. Goals are to talk through security, printing infrastructure setup & connectivity to Cloud Inventory, ports to open, etc. Resulting document is Architecture Design Documentation and the Customer Installation Master (CIM) for the customer to complete and return..
Ensure customer is set up for success regarding security access, printing infrastructure & cloud connectivity.
values.C13: Confirm ERP Version (i.e. tools release, 32- vs. 64-bit)
values.D13: Work with the customer to determine the version of their ERP we will be connecting with.
values.C14: Open CSC ticket to supply customer with product package associated with their ERP version (i.e. ASUs, BAPIs) if needed
values.D14: Based on the ERP & versioning details, work with Infrastructure and CSC to provide the customer the appropriate product package (e.g. JDE ASUs, SAP BAPIs, NetSuite Bundle, etc.)
values.C15: Request the data in the F9670 Software Update Master table, so ESU/ASU can be verified
values.D15: For JDE E1 customers that need upated ASUs, after they have been applied request the customer provide the data in the F9670 table to confirm it was deployed.
values.C16: Provide Customer Installation Master to Customer
values.D16: Following the ADW, Infrastructure consultant to provide the customer the CIM document to fill out prior to installation.
values.C17: Provide Architecture Design Document to Customer
values.D17: Following the ADW, Infrasructure consultant to provide the customer with the Architecture Design Document which outlines the proposed architecture discussed in the ADW meeting.
values.D18: As part of the ADW, infrastructure consultant to gather details around the customer's SSO setup in preparation for configuration within MEP (if in scope).
values.R19: Not Included - EPP Print Bridge Installation
values.D20:
High level project plan based on initial scope.
Allows project team(s) to better visualize project timeline.
values.D21:
This is done to hold correct resource. Does not have to be scheduled by task at this point. For on-prem customers, this task is dependent upon the customer providing an ETA on the CIM being returned and servers being provisioned.
Ensures resourcing can be as close as possible as early in project as possible.
values.H21: Request VPN & ERP Access / Onboarding Requirements
values.C22: Request VPN & ERP Access / Onboarding Requirements
values.D22: This task is for the PM to request the necessary access (ERP, DB, MEP, etc.) in order for the consultants to complete their work. This should be done as quickly as possible at the start of the project once resource have been identified in order to prevent delays in the project work getting started.
values.D23: This task is for the consultant(s) to confirm the access they've been provided is sufficient and allows them to complete their tasks.
values.C24: Create Shared Folder and Begin Project Status Reporting
values.D24:
The project status reporting is a weekly report that the project manager sends out. This report follows an existing template. This report is sent to account executive, the CSM, the executive sponsor, Technical Sponsor, PMO Manager, SA & DC.
Ensure entire project team is updated on weekly project changes.
values.C25: Finalize Customer Kickoff Presentation with Customer PM
values.D25: CI PM to work with customer to PM to ensure the slide deck is ready to jointly present to the project team prior to the kickoff meeting. All adjustments have been made and ownership of each slide has been designated for presenting.
values.D26:
Project kickoff meeting is led by the Project Manager & is focused on a presentation to customer team (usually 1-2 hours long). Best practice is to have this event on site. This includes the entire internal project team, sales team & customer team. Goal is to ensure customer is totally confident with implementation team & plan. If Delivery Consultant is resourced to project at this points its nice to have them listen in.
Ensure customer is totally confident with implementation team & plan.
values.D27: This task for the PMs from CI and the Customer to coordinate a cadence of executive alignment check-in meetings throughout the course of the project. Best practice is for this cadence to be monthly. Executive alignment calls are facilitated & scheduled by the project manager. Should include the PM, PMO Manager, Team/Project Lead, VP of PSO, and equivalent roles from customer.
values.D28:
Customer Administrative training is purely self-paced online training the that the customer admin is requried to complete. This is an important steps & must be completed prior to any testing starting. PM and CI team need to be sure to stress the importance of thsi training and the customer's system administration role. They will be responsible for monitoring integrations, transactions, triaging questions and issues, etc. If this role cannot be fulfilled by the customer, we should discuss long-term strategy internally and then with the customer and determine if additional service offerings are needed. Customer should also be encouraged to start using Cloud Inventory documentation portal & community pages as they are a great tool at this point in the project. The PM should check with the AE on the number of training licenses provided as part of the sale. Once the number of licenses and the specific users who will be going through the training are identified, the PM will need to create an access request in service desk (Service Desk > Service Catalog > Training > LMS User Access) https://servicedesk.nextworld.net/support/catalog/items/345
Ensure client admin users are given the basic training they need to be successful at this point in the project. Allows customer to get engaged via Cloud Inventory Doc Portal & Cloud Inventory Community pages.
values.D29:
The customer gateway and infrastructure set up is a customer task to get any of the action items that they have come out of that architecture Design workshop completed. Resulting actions might be setting up a gateway server, gaining access to network for printing, or if they're hosting any on prem ERPs we’ll need all access setup correctly for the install which should be documented by the customer in the Customer Installation Master (CIM).
Ensure customer has correct infrastructure in place prior to solution install occurring.
values.C30: Not Included - Enterprise Printing Platform Installation
values.D30: This task is for the infrastructure consultant to install the Enterprise Printing Platform. If on-premise, requires the customer to have provided a completed CIM and provisioned the necessary server according to specs provided in the ADW/ADD.
values.H30: Not Included - EPP Print Bridge Installation
values.C31: Not Included - EPP Print Bridge Installation
values.D31: This task is for the installation of the EPP print bridge (if required).This is typically used in the scenario where MEP is hosted in the cloud or in a different environment than where the printers are phsyically located and used to establish the connection between the two separate networks.
values.D32: CloudOps & infrastructure handles theMEP install. This task is the customer tenant being provisioned & the actual software installed. Ensure that the customer install contains MEPand EPP.
values.D33: This task is for the infrastructure consultant to register any tables and/or functions in MEP.
values.C34: Not Included - Ensure Language Text Files are Migrated
values.D34: This task is for the infrastructure consutlant to migrate any custom language text files from the customer's previous version of our product to the latest version as part of the upgrade process.
values.D35: This task is for the infrastructure consultant to migrate the existing users/roles from the client's existing MEP solution to the new instance, where applicable. If coming from an older version, users/roles may have to be created manually.
values.D36: This task is for the infrastructure consultant to work with the customer team to setup and configure Single-sign on to work with the customer's IdP.
values.D37: This task is for the Solution Architect to prep the application and necessary data components to be ready for the demonstation of applications with the customer.
values.D38: The site visit & walkthrough are for the Solution Architect, Project Manager, and Delivery Consultant (optional - depends on nature of the project). This event is to allow time to walk through client warehouse/facility, to identify their processes and get an understanding for how they're going to be using the solution. Findings are documented in real time. Ensure project team understands customers physical facility layout & can better visualize how software will be utilized.
values.D39: As a part of the site visit & walkthrough, detailed notes are taken. Generally, those notes are compiled & used to complete the solution Orientation session. A solution orientation session is where CI resources walk through the baselie applications/solution with the customer logged in to base Cloud Inventory following along. Ensure client has basic navigation skills in Cloud Inventory & has been oriented as to how the base transactions work. Client has been shown where customizations are likely to occur.
values.K39: Not Included - Business Requirement Document (BRD) Creation & Review Sessions
values.D40: The Pacejet Requirements session is a joint meeting with Pacejet, Cloud Inventory and the customer. It is advised that Cloud Inventory and Pacejet have a discussion following the requirements gathering session to review the requirements captured prior to hosting the call with the customer.
values.D41: Document created as a result of discussions that occurred at the Solution Orientation Session. Analysis to be used at executive alignment calls as needed. Ensure out of scope topics are captured effectively.
values.H41: Not Included - Business Requirement Document (BRD) Creation & Review Sessions
values.C42: Not Included - Business Requirement Document (BRD) Creation & Review Sessions
values.D42: BRD review sessions are typically led by the Solution Architect, Team Lead/Project Lead, Project Managers, & Delivery Consultant (optional). Goal is to work together to make sure customer fully understand the business requirements document and working towards sign off. And those are usually multiple (2-3) sessions to work through the BRD & get it ready for signoff. Ensure client is fully aware of the BRD components & working towards document signoff.
values.H42: Not Included - Business Requirement Document (BRD) Sign Off
values.C43: Not Included - Business Requirement Document (BRD) Sign Off
values.D43: CI sends the final draft of the BRD with a signature block to the signatory on the customer side and they execute it. Once signed any additional changes will result in change orders. Ensure client has signed BRD document to move project forward.
values.D44:
This is to take the high-level project plan and dates that we have been discussing up to this point, putting it into a final project plan with accurate resource bookings (task-level), contingencies built in, and then working with the customer project team to make sure that lines up with their dates, their resources, their expectations. At this point we will commit to the go live date and final project plan. This committed go-live date will be updated in OpenAir (Suite Projects).
Ensure initial project dates & requirements are accounted for in a final project plan that also aligns with client needs, establishing our committed go-live date.
values.D47:
Solution design is time for the solution architect to complete design work in Jira on any configurations of base apps or customizations identified as part of the BRD.
Ensure time allotted for design work to occur based on customer requirements.
values.H47: Not Included - Internal Solution Design Review
values.C48: Not Included - CI to Write Test Scripts (did not opt-in)
values.D48: If a customer opts-in for this added deliverable, CI would create test scripts for the customer based upon the signed requirements document. The Customer would then need to validate the test scripts and leverage them during testing.
values.D49: Client is to own the creation of test scripts. Typically, we will help Customer build test scripts based off the BRD and ensure the test cases cover end to end processes. Ensure client is comfortable writing test scripts & has capacity to do so. CI may provide templates or AI generated scripts based on the BRD.
values.D50:
Solution Architects will review the final customer test scripts and ensure they line up with the BRD and complete sign off. If this is not getting done, then it needs to be raised to the exec sponsors. 
Ensure alignment on client created test scripts.
values.C51: Not Included - Internal Solution Design Review
values.D51:
CI internal task, CI team works to ensure that documented processes were in fact the best way too solve for client issue/requests & identified problem were solved in an efficient way. CI team will be reviewing in Jira directly. This need sto include all DCs that will be working on the project, SA, PM, Project/Team Lead, and PMO manager.
Ensure alignment on project design documentation prior to project moving to next phase.
values.D54: Delivery Consultant works with the client to train them on how to get  scanners configured appropriately in accordance with the SOW, load the DSI mobile client & execute mobile apps on scanners. Ensure scanner requirements are identified, issues documented & configuration started.
values.H54: Not Included - Solution Workshop / Conference Room Pilot and Train the Trainer
values.D55: Delivery Consultant works to get printers setup in EPP per SOW. Ensure customer admin understand show to setup printers in MEP and EPP, and that the customer is actively working to test each type of printer model to be used in production and that the connection is established.
values.H55: Not Included - Solution Workshop / Conference Room Pilot and Train the Trainer
values.C56: Not Included - Ensure Temporary Licenses are in Place for New MEP Instance
values.D56: For upgrade projects, PM to work with Infrastructure Consultant, Account Executive, and CSC to ensure there are sufficient licenses in place for the new instance of MEP - both from a user licenses standpoint and platform license standpoint.
values.C57: Not Included - Verify List of Apps to be Migrated
values.D57: PM and Delivery Consultant to ensure the applications called out in the SOW match what the customer expects to be migrated. If additional applications are requested to be migrated, work with the customer and Account Executive through the change order process before migrating the additional applications.
values.C58: Review Apps with Data Replication with Project Lead Prior to Migration (if applicable)
values.D58: For upgrade projects, if there are any applications to be migrated that include data replication, have the Delivery Consultant work with the Project/Team Lead to review the Data Replication Rules, Tables, and Schedules prior to migrating the applications to ensure they migrate properly.
values.C60: Not Included - Base Application Package Install
values.C192: Not Included - Application Developer Training (did not opt-in)
values.D192: This is an add-on task customers can opt-in to where a CI Delivery Consultant helps a customer resource learn how to code within MEP.
values.D193: This task is for the customer to supply test data for the CI Delivery Consulant to use while Unit Testing.
values.H193: Unit Testing & QA  (hours included in application and/or upgrade estimates above)
values.C194: Unit Testing & QA  (hours included in application and/or upgrade estimates above)
values.D194: This task is for the Delivery Consultant to unit test the application(s) prior to hand-off to the customer for testing, leveraging the approved tset scripts for each application. For upgrade projects, unit testing is typically fairly limited and focuses on surface testing (i.e. the apps publish, can open without error, etc.) Unit Testing hours estimates are included in the individual application line items listed above.
values.D195:
Completed with technical leadership team, full review of applications built by Delivery Consultants. Code review and demo with the technical leadership team. This meeting/demo should include the SA, DC, PM, Project/Team Lead and PMO Manager.
Ensure applications are created and perform as designed; are functioning as intended without error.
values.D196: Customer task in which they work to create all users & roles as needed. DC to validate that the customer admin has set up users and roles correctly, typically results in Delivery Consultant assisting in the process. Ensure client has users & roles created correctly in preparation for go-live.
values.D197: Share an issues log and begin assigning issues to resources. Ensure client domain issues are captured & tracked correctly.
values.D198: This task is for the Delivery Consultant to demonstrate the Pacejet solution (if in scope) with the customer and confirm the solution is working as expected prior to UAT.
values.C199: Confirm resourcing & submit requests for UAT support (2-weeks prior to UAT)
values.D199: This task is for the PM to work with the customer to confirm UAT timing & details (e.g., on-site vs remote, testing plan/schedule, etc.) and align CI resources appropriately to support the event. Once the details are finalized, the PM will submit the necessary resource requests to ensure the event is supported appropriately.
values.D200:
Application Demonstrations are designed for the Delivery Consultant and Solution Architect to conduct hands on demonstrations walking client Super Users through the completed applications/integrations, end-to-end. Ideally, we group the demonstrations by process group/application set (Inbound, Inventory, Outbound). Best practice is to perform the walk through on customer devices. Leverage the approved test scripts as part of our walkthrough. Cloud Inventory to perform any issue remediation or address training items as needed. Any issues will be documented as an issue and tracked in Jira, associated with the application/integration where the problem occurred (use the 'Bug' issue type, but please note this does not indicate a product bug). These demonstrations are to occur iteratively throughout the development cycle as components of the process groups/applications sets are completed. 
Allows client Super Users & impacted customer stakeholders first hand exposure to the solutions and allows for feedback prior to customer testing/UAT. The goal is to get feedback as early as possible to allow enough time to make adjustments as needed. Note: any new requirements or out of scope changes need to be raised to customer PM and sponsor for CO approval before any action is taken to address them.
values.D201:
Review any/all remediation work that has occurred following the demonstrations to ensure solution set is ready for the Conference Room Pilot. Addressed items must be reviewed internally and if time allows, should be re-presented to the customer prior to the Conference Room Pilot.
Ensure that all takeaways from the initial solution workshops have been addressed in order to have a successful work.
values.H201: Not Included - Solution Workshop / Conference Room Pilot and Train the Trainer
values.C202: Not Included - Solution Workshop / Conference Room Pilot and Train the Trainer
values.D202:
The Solution Workshop / Conference Room Pilot is typically an on-site event where the SA, DC, and PM assist the customer to run through the Cloud Inventory solution we have created end-to-end, leveraging the customer-built test scripts. The customer super users will be executing the transactions on their devices/scanners that will be used in production. 
This exercise should be used for the Cloud Inventory team to train the super users on how to use the system, how to troubleshoot issues, and enable them to train the remaining UAT users and be the initial triage layer before reporrting issues back to Cloud Inventory. This is the intial transfer of ownership of the solution from Cloud Inventory to the customer.

values.D204: This  task is for the PM to work with the Account Executive, Delivery Consultant, CSC, anad customer to confirm the appropriate amount of user or device licenses are configured in the Test environment prior to testing. The goal is to ensure adequate licenses are available to match the number of users that will be testing as well as for the consultant(s) suporting the event.
values.C207: Confirm resourcing & submit requests for Go-live support (2-weeks prior to Go-live)
values.D207: This task is for the PM to work with the customer to confirm Go-live timing & details (e.g., on-site vs remote, cutover plan/schedule, etc.) and align CI resources appropriately to support the event. values.C208: Not Included - Develop End User Documentation (did not opt-in)

values.C209: Select & Introduce User Acceptance Testing (UAT) Users
values.D209: Customer to select and train the User Acceptance Testing users. These users play a part in the final validation of the software. This training likely has large overlap with Solution workshop training events. Ensure client has identified who the UAT users will be & that they are comfortable navigating the solution effectively.
values.D210: Create & finalize detailed UAT agenda outlining what apps are being tested & when with the customer team. Create PPT presentation for user testing kickoff event. Ensure UAT event is outlined & app testing sequence identified.
values.D211: This task is for the Solution Architect, Delivery Consultant, and PM to work with the customer to ensure enough data is prepared for the UAT testing team to execute all of the UAT test scripts during the UAT window.
values.D212: User Acceptance Testing event is designed to allow client users to test their solutions on the floor with devices setup and printers configured. Delivery Consultant are asked to support as issues might arise & all issues get put on an issues log and assigned to the dedicated resource to remediate. PM & DC will facilitate the session and issues logging.
values.D213: Once User Acceptance Testing is complete, client will sign off confirming issues are resolved & event is complete. Provides written confirmation & client agreement the event was successful.
values.D214: Project manager schedules meeting with Customer Support Center team. This introduction meeting is a quick introduction & presentation covering solution support. This meeting occurs prior to any applications going into client’s production envionment. Serves as customers first look at post go-live support structure & allows for questions to ensure client is confident in support process.
values.C215: Not Included - CI Led End User Training (did not opt-in)

values.D216: Previously trained client Trainers & Super Users to complete all additional customer End User Training. Ensure customer has a plan to successfully train all end users & completes training on time for all new solutions.

The ESTIMATE and ESTIMATE DETAIL pages build to the Calculations page.  There is some consilidation here. There are considerable calculations based off the development effort.

Open the existing estimate
create a new blank workbook
change the name of the sheet in the new workbook to "Schedule" same as the original workbook

Paste formatting into the new sheet
Paset (just paste) into the new sheet
go to formulas and Name Manager
change the reference of task start and task end to just the local sheet
Delete the name SCH_STATUS
Go down the column of Billagle Hours Budgeted and chang from the current formula reference to just the same value entered in the cell (i.e. current formula may be "=Calculations!E9+Calculations!H9" and show a value of 10  You would change it to just be 10
You will do this for all values greater than blank (i.e. you need to update all the zero values to zero)  Leave blanks as blank
You should now be able to enter a start date and enter dates in task start / task end and see the gant chart update.

values.B51: Where a Customer is asking only for a budgetary number use this to establish a high value for the project range
values.B53: Markup will add a percentage to a project total based on services team perspective of client, deliverables and other soft factors.  The total of each phase will be totaled and the selected markup factor will be applied.  this shows in the schedlue as will show hours from the various sections as a result of the calculations.  For a standard delivery, the standard and optional hours will be shown.   For a phase 0 the phase 0 and delivery phase hours will be shown.  Note that in either case the total hours will be rounded to a number of days
values.B55: A timeline for the project based on typical assumptions
values.B57: This page is where each base application, customer application, label, interface is detailed out.  There will be a base number which is protected and is a result of the entries on the ESTIMATE page.   You can change the mod hours in any category.  For labels and interfaces expectation is you would provide details here (i.e. label for PO with 10 elements) that would assist in the continunity of passing detail to the services team.   Each category of the project will have a total hours and a total count that will be incorporated into the calculations page or the schedule page.
values.B59: The ESTIMATE and ESTIMATE DETAIL pages build to the Calculations page.  There is some consilidation here.  As an example all the baseline application development hours are consolidated to a single value.  You can override hours (Standard Adjust)Where the retuls (Standard Extended) hours is what is carried back to the ESTIMATE page.  There is a small section of Plan not Billed hours where for Cloud installs the platform install task are moved here where they are not billable but contingency and project managment hours consider these hours.  There are considerable calculations based off the development effort.
values.B61:
Page constins schedule for Implementation managers.  This is populated from the Calculations page for many of the task.  The customer name will populate from the estimate sheet.  The Implementation manager should fill in their name.  The hours caclculated for governance and oversight are shown here also. 
There are columns for the task name, the designated persona, the  status of the task / phase, the percentage complete (carried at a phase level) the hours budgeted (populated from calcualtions page or entered) a column to enter hours from change orders, the hours used for the task (accumulates at a phase level) the hours used against the task / phase, The hours remaining in the task / phase, The health of the taks / phase The estimate at completion, comments and a set of columns for setting start / stop dates

You can break out the schedule to a separte page by doing the following. 
Open the existing estimate
create a new blank workbook
change the name of the sheet in the new workbook to "Schedule" same as the original workbook
Copy the entire existing Schedule Page by clicking the triangel in the intersecting corner of row / columns
Paste formatting into the new sheet
Paset (just paste) into the new sheet
go to formulas and Name Manager
change the reference of task start and task end to just the local sheet
Delete the name SCH_STATUS
Go down the column of Billagle Hours Budgeted and chang from the current formula reference to just the same value entered in the cell (i.e. current formula may be "=Calculations!E9+Calculations!H9" and show a value of 10  You would change it to just be 10
You will do this for all values greater than blank (i.e. you need to update all the zero values to zero)  Leave blanks as blank
You should now be able to enter a start date and enter dates in task start / task end and see the gant chart update.
